---
title: "Billing"
description: "Initial credits, billing pods, and getting a Google Cloud billing account at Yale"
---

Everything you run in the Workbench (apps, queries, storage) costs money. It's paid for through a **pod**.

## Initial credits

- **\$300 in initial credits** per registered researcher
  - Applied automatically to compute costs
  - **Expire 365 days** after you first get Workbench access
  - Tied to your personal pod, **`user-pod-firstname-lastname-####`**. A workspace's **Workspace details** panel (right side, under **Pod**) shows which pod pays for it.
- When credits run out or expire:
  - You can't launch or open analysis environments
  - Stored resources (buckets, disks) **may be deleted**

::: {.callout-important}
Set up a **Google Cloud billing account** and **billing pod** *before* your credits run out or expire. At Yale, ask **at least 2 to 3 weeks ahead**: see [Getting a Google Cloud billing account at Yale](#getting-a-google-cloud-billing-account-at-yale).
:::

## Billing pods

- A **pod** connects your workspaces to a Google Cloud billing account
  - Workspace costs are charged to the pod
  - Think of the pod as your billing account inside the Workbench
- One pod can pay for **many workspaces**
- You can **invite other users** to your pod (e.g., lab members). Their workspaces in your pod are then billed to **your** account
- All of Us researchers have the **Pod Manager** role, so you can create your own pod

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out"}
- A pod links to only **one** billing account
- A workspace's pod **can't be changed** later. To switch pods, you have to duplicate the workspace.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Instructor tip"}
Initial credits are linked to the personal user pod. Check a workspace's Workspace details panel (Overview tab, right side) to see which pod it uses; a Yale billing pod would show its own name there.
:::

## Getting a Google Cloud billing account at Yale

::: {.callout-important title="Ask early"}
Setting up the account takes about **2 weeks**: Burwood, Yale's Google reseller, requests it from Google's distributor. Ask **at least 2 to 3 weeks** before your initial credits run out or expire.
:::

Email **cloud.support\@yale.edu** with the subject **"setting up an All of Us billing account"** and include:

- Your All of Us Workbench email (e.g., `yourname@researchallofus.org`)
- Your **COA** number: the account is charged to it
- Whether this is an **NIH-funded** project, and if so, the **NIH grant number**. NIH-funded accounts are set up through **NIH STRIDES**, which needs it

Yale Cloud Support will send the next steps for linking the Google Cloud billing account and creating your **pod**.

### What you get

- **Your own** Google Cloud billing account, charged to the COA you gave
- You **keep access** to it, so you can link it to new pods, or relink pods, yourself, without asking Yale Cloud Support again

::: {.callout-warning title="Choose who you invite to your pod"}
Anyone you invite to your pod can run workspaces that are billed to **your COA**. Invite only people on the **same grant**.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Instructor tip"}
Email is the way to ask for now. Yale Cloud Support is building a **ServiceNow** request form for this; link it here when it's live. Yale Cloud Support may give additional or different guidance.
:::
